title: Contracts
audience: a law student in a U.S. JD program
purpose: Analyze contract formation (offer, acceptance, consideration and its substitutes), defenses, the statute of frauds, interpretation and the parol evidence rule, conditions, performance and breach, remedies, third parties, and UCC Article 2 sales.
primary_reading: Cornell LII: Uniform Commercial Code Article 2 and the Wex legal dictionary

weeks.5: Defenses: capacity, duress, misrepresentation and unconscionability
weeks.8: Interpretation and the parol evidence rule
weeks.10: Impossibility, impracticability and frustration of purpose

blocks.deliverable: Brief three offer-and-acceptance cases and apply them to a new problem.
Decide whether five promises are enforceable and on what basis.
Write an IRAC answer to a mistake problem.
Week 7 midterm; apply the statute of frauds to six agreements.
Analyze a material-breach problem with express conditions.
Compute expectation damages with mitigation and foreseeability limits.
Submit the project; take an unseen 180 minute final in week 14.

project: Contract dispute memo: from a supplied file of emails, a purchase order and a delivery record, write a 2,000-word memo on formation, terms, breach and remedies under the UCC and the common law, then draft a short settlement letter.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
